title: Alaska Airlines named presenting sponsor of the Woodland Park Gran Prix, the world’s largest one-day cyclocross race
summary: Seattle’s hometown airline joins MFG Cyclocross for its season finale on Sunday, November 22, in Lower Woodland Park.
body_markdown:
*Seattle’s hometown airline joins MFG Cyclocross for its season finale on Sunday, November 22, in Lower Woodland Park*


**SEATTLE** — Off Camber Productions, organizer of MFG Cyclocross, today announced that Alaska Airlines will be the presenting sponsor of the 2026 Woodland Park Gran Prix. The race, on Sunday, November 22, in Seattle’s Lower Woodland Park, has been the largest one-day cyclocross race in the world four years running. It drew over 1,000 racers in 2024 and 2025.


As presenting sponsor, Alaska Airlines will have a presence across race day. In addition to a hosted tent, the airline will provide airline tickets and Atmos Rewards points as race prizes and run giveaways for racers throughout the event.


“Woodland Park has become Seattle’s biggest day on a bike each fall, and the largest one-day cyclocross race on the planet,” said Erik Olson, principal of Off Camber Productions. “Having Seattle’s hometown airline as our presenting sponsor is a perfect fit. Alaska shares our belief that this sport is for everyone, from kids on their first lap to elite racers, and we can’t wait to welcome them to the park.”


“More than 11,000 employees at Alaska, Horizon, and Hawaiian call Seattle home, and showing up in the community as Seattle’s only hometown global airline is important to us,” said Eric Edge, Vice President of Marketing and Guest Experience at Alaska Airlines. “We are excited to be involved in this year’s Woodland Park Gran Prix, and we look forward to seeing everyone at the starting line this weekend.”


The Woodland Park Gran Prix runs from 9am through mid-afternoon, with seven race waves for all ages and abilities, from kids’ races to elite fields. Registration and event details are at[mfgcyclocross.bike](https://mfgcyclocross.bike/) .


### About MFG Cyclocross and Off Camber Productions


MFG Cyclocross is the largest cyclocross series in North America, hosting three of the top five biggest cyclocross races in the US in 2025. The six-race fall series has run in and around Seattle since 2009, and the Woodland Park Gran Prix is its finale. MFG Cyclocross is produced by Off Camber Productions, a Seattle event company that also runs The GRiT adventure gravel ride in the Cascades.


### About Alaska, Hawaiian and Horizon


Alaska Airlines, Hawaiian Airlines and Horizon Air are subsidiaries of Alaska Air Group, and McGee Air Services is a subsidiary of Alaska Airlines. We are a global airline with hubs in Seattle, Honolulu, Portland, Anchorage, Los Angeles, San Diego and San Francisco. We deliver remarkable care as we fly our guests to more than 140 destinations throughout North America, Latin America, Asia, the Pacific and Europe. Guests can book travel at[alaskaair.com](https://www.alaskaair.com/) and[hawaiianair.com](https://www.hawaiianairlines.com/) . Alaska and Hawaiian are members of the oneworld© alliance. Members of our[Atmos™ Rewards](https://www.alaskaair.com/atmosrewards) loyalty program can earn and redeem points with oneworld airlines and our additional global partners that serve over 1,100 worldwide destinations. Learn more about what’s happening at Alaska and Hawaiian at[news.alaskaair.com](https://news.alaskaair.com/) . Alaska Air Group is traded on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) as “ALK.”
